Operational estimate, not physiological measurement: 220 - age, the observed lower bound, a declared maximum, custom limits and the 65/81/89/97 bands are a reference scale only; zone model confidence LOW; no zone edge is a threshold.
Age estimate only for an age in force of 18-80 (AGE_OUTSIDE_ESTIMATE_RANGE past it); extending the population is a Founder / G01 decision.

Display-only reference: effort and pace govern every session; heart rate never changes the plan and is never primary, a target, a gate, a dose, progression, pace-band, estimate, medical evidence or safety-release input; a slow-down cue only from Z4 in EASY, LONG, RECOVERY_EASY, SHAKEOUT and (in EASY mode only) EASY_REESTABLISHMENT; never a cue to speed up.

QRE-HR5R-07 week rule: each easy-running session's cue is resolved over its own week's measured references (weekMeasuredReferences) with the profile in force; a measured reference reaches a provisional session of a later week only, never the week in force; the athlete's declared maximum, custom limits and their erasure apply to every week at once (an explicit athlete choice that changes no plan).
HR5R-C1: an unused qualifying chest-strap maximum more than 5 bpm above a declared maximum is shown beside it; the override is never replaced automatically.
HR5R-C2: under REFERENCE_CONFLICT, both measured values and the reference used are shown, with the option to enter one's own maximum.
HR5R-C3: the age-estimate disclosure keeps both the magnitude and the older-adult direction of the error, and 'You can enter your own'.
HR5R-C4: the cue keeps 'consider slowing down' and 'a low reading never means speed up'; no alarm styling, no health meaning.
HR5R-C5: a cue on an estimated or declared maximum carries that reference's disclosure and is never shown as a personal limit.
HR5R-C6: no live cue before a live heart-rate channel has its own SSCTR and Data review defining 'sustained'.

HR5R-C7: one heart-rate cue per session; where the five zones are AVAILABLE the five-zone Z4 cue is presented and the three-zone conservativeCueOnly is not presented as a second cue; the two scales are never presented as one (a presentation rule; the frozen three-zone bytes stay unchanged).
HR5R-C8: zones are named Z1-Z5 or with neutral effort words, never 'Tempo', 'Threshold' or 'Anaerobic'.
HR5R-C9: a classified single value is shown as the highest recorded heart rate in a zone, with its sensor (and the OPTICAL_MEASUREMENT disclosure when optical), never as time in a zone.

HR5R-C10: time in zone stays UNAVAILABLE; the classifier's numeric defaults are unwired placeholders, not approved rules; a heart-rate series channel requires its own SSCTR and Data review (limits, artifacts, cadence lock, plausibility floor, warm-up, sampling).
HR5R-C11: no heart-rate reading suggests rest, illness or overtraining; symptoms stay on the existing warning-sign route.

HR5R-C12: medication or conditions that alter heart rate remain ASK / ELIGIBILITY_UNASSESSED and CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED for any individual judgement; whether a generic nonclinical statement is shown is for the clinical owner and Product, routed by Chief.
HR5R-C13: heart-rate, lab and HealthKit values are health-adjacent data: Security and privacy review before any real athlete.
An AI reviewer's provisional internal sporting judgement, not human, clinical or empirical validation.
Proposed for funded human revalidation under HQ-V1HR5R-SSCTR-ZONES (linked to HQ-V1HR5-SSCTR-ZONES and HQ-V1RC-SSCTR-HR), appended by Founder or Chief.
Review by 2027-05-11 or earlier on the triggers of SSCTR-HR5R-DECISION-r1.
